title: The wrong-coloured bishop

D0.outcome: Explains why a rook pawn with a bishop that does not control the queening corner can draw: the defending king in the corner holds.

D1.outcome: Told the bishop's colour and the pawn's file, predicts win or draw.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled endings, tells win from draw for the family (pawn on a or h, bishop colour, defender king distance) and finds the king route.

D3.outcome: Verifies each claim with the tablebase and predicts the effect of a second pawn or a different file.

sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.1.md §4 (wrong and right-coloured bishop positions verified)
conditions: A rook pawn; the bishop does not control the queening square; the defender's king can reach the corner.
The right-coloured bishop wins (verified win in 29).
contrasts: The same set-up with the right-coloured bishop, or with a non-rook pawn.
Thinking an extra bishop always wins.
A pawn not on the edge.
